section_summary: This section of State Department decimal file 894.413 covers the administration, surveillance, and documentation of monuments, statues, and cultural properties in occupied Japan between March 1947 and October 1949. It details Eighth Army and Japanese ministerial directives prohibiting militaristic ceremonies and monuments, Department of State efforts to acquire SCAP Civil Information and Education (CIE) Section records and microfilms, and comprehensive investigations into the January 1949 fire that damaged the ancient murals of Horyuji. It also includes reporting and press coverage on the dedication of a monument in Yokohama honoring missionary Dr. James Curtis Hepburn, as well as an unrelated administrative note.

subfiles.about: Forwards Eighth Army Operational Directive No. 21 and Japanese ministerial notifications regarding public funerals and war monuments.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch forwarding Eighth Army Operational Directive No. 21 and Japanese ministerial notifications regarding war memorials and ceremonies.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 910: Funerals, Memorial Services, and Monuments for War Dead, Militarists and Ultranationalists

subfiles.about: Establishes Occupation policies and regulations prohibiting official sponsorship of ceremonies and monuments for the war dead, militarists, and ultranationalists.
subfiles.from: Headquarters, Eighth Army
subfiles.summary: Headquarters Eighth Army directive regulating ceremonies and monuments for war dead and militarists, prohibiting official sponsorship or public facility use, banning new memorials, and ordering removal of militaristic statues from schools and public grounds.
subfiles.title: Operational Directive No. 21: Funerals, Memorial Services, and Monuments for War Dead, Militarists and Ultranationalists

subfiles.title: Notification A No. 73: Disposition of Monuments and Statues

subfiles.from: Vice-Minister of Home Affairs and Vice-Minister of Education
subfiles.summary: Joint ministerial notification enforcing separation of religion and state by prohibiting local government bodies from sponsoring funerals or ceremonies for war dead, while permitting secular honors for those dying in civilian duty.
subfiles.title: Joint Notification No. 51: Public Funerals, etc.
subfiles.to: Governors of Prefectures, and Presidents and Directors of Universities, Colleges, and High Schools

subfiles.summary: Sample master card index entry detailing Kinta Muto's private art collection and summarizing inspections conducted by occupation personnel.

subfiles.about: Provides a sample Master Card Index entry documenting National Treasure structures, objects, damage, and repair estimates for Jingu-ji temple.

subfiles.summary: Sample master card index entry documenting registered national treasure structures at Jingu-ji, noting structural deterioration, and estimating repair costs.
subfiles.title: Sample of Master Card Index: Registered Site (Jingu-ji)

subfiles.about: Summarizes weekly activities of the Arts and Monuments Division, including agency developments, field examiner operations, Korean protection, and general matters.

subfiles.summary: Weekly report of the Arts and Monuments Division covering museum transfers, National Treasures law revisions, field examiner recruitment, and Korean collection issues.
subfiles.title: Weekly Report of Arts and Monuments Division for Week Ending 7 February 1947
subfiles.to: Chief, Civil Information and Education Section

subfiles.about: Reports on the physical condition, preservation problems, and administrative neglect of cultural, artistic, and historic sites in Shizuoka Prefecture.
subfiles.from: C. F. Gallagher, Field Inspector
subfiles.summary: Field inspector C. F. Gallagher reports on his inspection of cultural, artistic, and historic sites throughout Shizuoka Prefecture conducted in late January 1947. The report documents inadequate protection, neglected national treasures, and severe fire risks at various temples and shrines, including the poor maintenance of Townsend Harris's historic residence at Gyokusenji. It recommends establishing Gyokusenji as an international monument, reminding local custodians of their legal responsibilities, and registering additional Kamakura sculptures.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Report on Inspection of Shizuoka Prefecture

subfiles.about: Reports on liaison with Japanese government agencies, art institutions, protection of structures and objects, and national park budgeting.
subfiles.from: Sherman E. Lee, Acting Chief, Arts and Monuments Division
subfiles.summary: Weekly report covering liaison with the Ministry of Education, National Museum exhibitions, municipal and private museums, shrine repair budgets, and art export clearances.
subfiles.title: Weekly Report of Arts and Monuments Division for Week Ending 26 September 1947

subfiles.summary: Field examination report documenting the history, architectural condition, and Buddhist statues of Okuraji temple in Nara Prefecture.
subfiles.title: Report 146: Okuraji (Daizoji)

subfiles.about: Requests an urgent report and photographs on the extent of fire damage to the Horyuji Golden Hall and wall frescoes.

subfiles.summary: Airgram requesting an immediate report and photographs regarding fire damage to the Horyuji Golden Hall and wall frescoes.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-29: Request for Report on Damage to Horyuji Kondo and Frescoes
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Reports that CIE is preparing a report on the Horyuji fire from Japanese sources and has ordered damage photographs.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Airgram reporting that CIE is translating Japanese reports on the Horyuji fire and procuring official photographs of the damage.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-51: Fire Damage to Horyu Temple

subfiles.about: Transmits the official Ministry of Education report on fire damage to the Golden Hall and murals of Horyuji.
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, for Acting Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch transmitting the Ministry of Education's official report on fire damage sustained by the Horyuji Golden Hall.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 162: Fire Damage to Horyu Temple

subfiles.about: Details the fire damage sustained by the Kondo and twelve murals of Horyuji, its cause, and emergency restoration countermeasures.
subfiles.from: Cultural Section, School Education Bureau, Ministry of Education
subfiles.summary: This official Ministry of Education report details the devastating fire of January 26, 1949 inside the Kondo (Golden Hall) of Horyuji in Nara Prefecture. It documents the pre-fire dismantling status, the probable ignition caused by electric heating cushions, and provides an itemized damage assessment for all twelve ancient wall murals and their ongoing reproductions. The report also establishes emergency conservation procedures, a reconstruction schedule through 1951, and administrative responsibilities under the National Treasures Preservation Law.
subfiles.title: Report: Damage of the Horyuji Kondo and Measures Taken

subfiles.about: Transmits twelve official National Museum photographs of the fire damage sustained by the twelve wall murals of Horyuji Kondo.
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, for Acting Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch transmitting twelve official National Museum photographs documenting fire damage to the mural paintings of Horyuji's Golden Hall.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 178: Transmitting Photographs of Fire Damage to Horyu Temple, Nara, Japan

subfiles.about: Visual documentation showing the fire damage and pigment peeling on the twelve ancient mural paintings of Horyuji Kondo.
subfiles.from: Official Photographer, National Museum, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: A collection of eleven photographic plates showing the extent of fire damage to the twelve wall murals inside the Kondo of Horyuji. Prepared by the official photographer of the National Museum, these plates illustrate the severe charring, discoloration, and plaster peeling caused by the January 1949 fire. They were transmitted to Washington to provide visual documentation of the cultural loss.
subfiles.title: Photographs of Fire Damage to Horyu Temple Murals

subfiles.about: Transmits eight spools of microfilm containing the Ministry of Education's List of Works, Collections, Sites and Installations Requiring Protection.
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch transmitting eight microfilm spools containing the complete List of Works, Collections, Sites and Installations Requiring Protection.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 222: Forwarding Materials Regarding Japanese Arts and Monuments

subfiles.about: Explains Department needs for CIE weekly reports in Far Eastern restitution policy and expresses gratitude for Horyuji fire reports and photographs.
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Airgram detailing why the Department needs CIE weekly reports for Far Eastern cultural restitution policy, and commending received Horyuji reports.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-118: Request for Arts and Monuments Weekly Reports and Other Cultural Property Documents
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Reports that CIE refused to release its weekly reports but will allow USPOLAD to survey and copy file materials.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Airgram reporting CIE's refusal to release weekly reports, offering a survey of division files, and noting a planned war-damage brochure.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-257: Arts and Monuments Weekly Reports

subfiles.about: Reports on the unveiling in Yokohama of a monument and bronze plaque commemorating missionary Dr. James Curtis Hepburn.
subfiles.from: James B. Pilcher, American Consul General, Yokohama

subfiles.title: Newspaper Clippings: "Hepburn Plaque to be Unveiled" and "Hepburn Anniversary"
